analysis.title: Global Credit Trader: Taking Stock of Performance and Where to Invest From Here
key_insights: Credit performance has been challenged in recent months. HY has not benefited as much as IG from the rally in rates since October 5. Among the largest actively managed funds, the past month was uniformly challenging across IG and HY versus benchmark.

Since mid-October, AI-related cost-of-capital concerns have spilled into the non-AI market. Spreads decompressed (lower-rated cohorts underperformed) and correlations rose. Treasuries rallied as a hedge amid the risk-off tone.

GS's answer to whether the macro backdrop supports performing non-AI credit is a 'qualified yes'. The baseline macro view is benign, but the left tail of the growth distribution is thicker. Valuations are far from cheap historically, so GS does not view broad-based dip buying as prudent.
USD pairwise spread-change correlations reached their highest level since the 1Q2026 Iran escalation. EUR credit correlations also rose with sovereign bond volatility in the Euro area.

USD: GS expects compression in non-AI IG and favors BBBs over higher-rated peers. It sees the recent non-AI decompression as an opportunity to position for compression. It does not extend the BBB view to HY.

HY has traded in three parts: AI-related, performing HY, and distressed. GS is neutral on HY AI-related credit, especially project finance structures (underwriting-dependent but with an attractive yield). It is underweight CCCs because higher rates, elevated input costs and idiosyncratic pressures create macro and refinancing stress.

Within performing HY, GS expects BBs to absorb most future AI-related financing and any duration headwind, so it prefers carry in single-Bs. It expects dispersion within single-Bs to rise because there is little room for fundamental error.

For crossover investors, GS prefers moving down in capital structure seniority (subordination premium) over moving down in credit quality. Corporate hybrids and money center bank subordinated debt screen attractive after the recent widening.

Low-AI-correlation sectors are the new defensives. In IG, Utilities, Financials and Healthcare/Pharma show lower correlation to AI-related spreads. In HY, Energy also stands out. GS calls adding them a prudent risk management tool.

EUR credit has benefited from little AI-related issuance, but elevated energy prices and sovereign and fiscal risks pushed spreads wider. GS prefers USD over EUR credit and advocates defensive positioning, geographic diversification and awareness of the macro left tail.

In EUR, Banks are the main conduit for sovereign risk and have underperformed non-financials even excluding France. GS stays underweight French Banks but is constructive on the broader regional Banks sector. It does not expect senior bank spreads to revisit the 2011-12 sovereign crisis wides.

In EUR HY, GS recommends a defensive ratings mix and prefers moving up in quality. A steeper maturity wall makes elevated rates more of a refinancing story, and growth-sensitive sectors trade with little premium.

Macro credit index hedges are still worth holding. Implied volatility is near post-COVID medians in USD credit and at the 65th percentile in EUR credit. Skew has flattened and the term structure is flatter, which favors outright payers and longer-dated hedges. GS says a better entry point to add hedges may come soon.

Fund screen, USD IG: the 20 largest funds hold $345B, with only five actively managed. They are -0.5% YTD and +1.5% over one month, helped by the rate rally. Actively managed IG funds have a YTD excess return of -0.2% after a -0.7% excess return last month.

Fund screen, USD HY: the 20 largest funds hold $202B, with eleven actively managed. They returned +0.6% over one month, -0.9% over three months and +0.2% YTD through Oct 28. Actively managed HY funds have +0.9% YTD excess return on carry, offset by -0.6% last month.

Relative value views: overweight USD vs EUR, neutral IG vs HY, overweight BBBs, overweight Bs, neutral BBs, underweight CCCs, overweight HY bonds vs loans, overweight CLO mezzanine tranches vs leveraged loans, overweight hybrids vs BBBs, and prefer Agency MBS vs IG. GS now sees the case for an outright IG overweight as less obvious on valuations, rate sensitivity and supply technicals.

In the EUR market GS is overweight BBBs, overweight HY bonds vs loans, and overweight BBs while neutral Bs and underweight CCCs. It is overweight EUR IG CLO tranches vs USD IG CLO tranches. It prefers HY bonds over loans because of the loan market's software weighting and the 2028 maturity wall.
Spread forecasts: USD IG 86bp now, 80bp for 2026Q4, 78bp 2027Q1 and 2027Q2 (as printed in the dashboard). USD HY 312bp now, 290bp then 280bp. EUR IG 103bp now. EUR HY 378bp now.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight BBB USD IG vs higher-rated cohorts (AA and A), positioning for compression after non-AI decompression
trade_ideas.rationale: Recent underperformance in non-AI IG offers an entry to position for compression, and GS sees possible balance sheet deterioration at the highest end of the rating spectrum.
trade_ideas.risk: Valuations are tight by historical standards and the growth left tail is thicker.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight single-B HY for carry, underweight CCCs, neutral BBs
trade_ideas.rationale: BBs are expected to absorb AI-related financing supply and any duration headwind, while CCCs face macro and refinancing stress.
trade_ideas.risk: Dispersion within single-Bs is expected to rise and there is little room for fundamental error.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight corporate hybrids vs BBBs and money center bank subordinated (tier 2) debt
trade_ideas.rationale: Recent widening gives an entry point to take subordinated risk while growth is 'good enough' and capital markets are open. GS expects the hybrid premium to compress as the market grows.
trade_ideas.risk: Subordinated risk if the macro baseline deteriorates.

trade_ideas.description: Hold macro credit index hedges, adding protection on local rallies
trade_ideas.rationale: Macro hedges proved effective when AI funding stress hit aggregate demand and spreads moved together. Flatter skew and term structure improve payoff economics.
trade_ideas.risk: Implied volatility is near post-COVID medians in USD, so hedging has become more expensive.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight CLO mezzanine tranches (BB and BBB) vs leveraged loans, and use spread widening to add CLO exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: Historical data shows low impairment rates for BB and BBB CLO tranches, and valuations offer carry and a cushion against moderate to elevated defaults.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher default outcomes than the cushion absorbs.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight USD credit vs EUR credit, and overweight HY bonds vs loans in both regions
trade_ideas.rationale: The Euro Area has a more challenging growth, inflation and monetary policy mix. Loan markets are heavily weighted to software, with the 2028 maturity walls unresolved.
trade_ideas.risk: Cross-border issuance is blurring the regional distinction.

risk_factors: AI-related funding needs over a multi-year period, with supply indigestion in lower-rated AI borrowers.
A thicker left tail of the growth distribution.
Valuations are tight by historical standards.
Higher rates, elevated input costs and idiosyncratic pressures create refinancing stress in CCCs.
Dispersion within single-Bs is expected to rise.
Euro Area sovereign and fiscal risks, especially France, with Banks as the conduit.
Elevated energy prices weigh on EUR credit.
A steeper EUR HY maturity wall turns elevated rates into a refinancing story.
Potential duration headwinds if rates drift higher.
Software exposure in the loan market and 2028 loan maturity walls.

tension_points.bull_case: The baseline macro view is benign and 'good enough' for higher-quality credit, particularly in the U.S. Recent non-AI spread widening offers more attractive entry points, and capital markets remain open for high quality issuers.
tension_points.bear_case: The left tail of the growth distribution is thicker, valuations are still tight by historical standards, and AI-related cost-of-capital concerns can threaten the broader growth narrative. GS does not favor broad-based dip buying.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A threshold of AI-related funding stress that disrupts aggregate demand, as seen since mid-October, would hit the broader market. GS does not state a specific level.
